notes: The ONE connector config for intraday_poc.connectors:AlpacaBarsConnector, validated default-deny against its spec(), and the one BOTH acquisition modes run through. Register once, then acquire in either mode: python -m dskit.onboarding register-source alpaca --catalog-source alpaca-src --connector intraday_poc.connectors:AlpacaBarsConnector --config @configs/source-backfill.json --activate; then --mode backfill for the history and --mode live for the forward top-up. RULING (2026-08-28, hardcoding audit): ONE SOURCE NAME, two modes. ADR-0014 keys checkpoints per (source, stream, MODE), so the two pulls already hold independent cursors without a second registration — while observations live at observations/<source>/ and a run document reads exactly ONE source, so the second source name this child used to ship (alpaca-live) put every live-acquired bar in a tree the documents never read: no error, just an unused store. One name also keeps the store homogeneous — one feed, one adjustment, one price series per (symbol, ts), which is what the model is fit on. live_lookback_minutes is what that ruling costs and how it is paid: the live mode's cursor is empty until its own first pull, and windowing that from start below would re-fetch every bar since 2021 and commit them as a SECOND full acquisition — the bitemporal dedup keeps the model's view right (latest acquired_at wins per (symbol, ts)), but every later scan would then carry two copies of the whole store. Bounded to a day, the first live pull covers the seam instead of repeating the backfill. The trade-off IS that seam: bars older than this window and newer than the backfill's cursor belong to no pull, so widen the knob or let the backfill catch up to within it before switching live on. feed=sip because the free tier serves FULL consolidated-tape history (back to 2016) — the IEX-only restriction is a real-time restriction, not a historical one; the connector clamps the fetch window 16 minutes into the past to clear the free tier's SIP gate, which is also why a live-mode pull trails the tape by ~16 minutes. adjustment=all (splits + dividends) keeps the return series stationary for the model, and the forward loop READS it from this file (live.py --source-config) so the series it serves on is adjusted the way the trained one was; symbols is read the same way, so the loop trades exactly the universe that was acquired. The one vendor knob the loop cannot take from here is the feed, because real-time SIP is not sold on the free tier (README, 'What to know before trusting the numbers'). Store a second source with adjustment=raw if as-traded fills ever matter. That same clamp bounds live_lookback_minutes from below on this feed: 16 or less would window from now-lookback to now-16min — an empty window on every pull, nothing acquired, nothing said — so the gate refuses that combination outright. Secrets are env-var NAMES (key_env/secret_env defaults apply) — the material never enters this file, a snapshot, or any hash — and the forward loop reads THESE names too, so pointing them at another account here moves both sides. Both sides also run ONE rule for what counts as a credential (connectors.resolve_credentials): a name that is missing OR set to the empty string is refused BY NAME, never authenticated — .env.example ships both keys empty, so a presence-only check would have let a blank pair reach the broker. What the two do NOT share is where the values come from: the puller's connector reads the process environment only, while the forward loop also reads .env beside its CWD (dskit's env.py, process environment winning). Export the pair — set -a; . ./.env; set +a — and both acquire and live.py are served.
